Do you care about animals and sustainability? Do you love using social media? Would you like a job focused on using social media to make the world a better place for animals and the environment?

We are currently looking for a new Social Media Manager to join our team, who will be in charge of running multiple social media accounts on platforms including but not limited to Facebook and Instagram.

At Axon, we're committed to our mission of Protecting Life. We stand at the forefront of tackling society's most pressing safety and justice challenges. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other. We are on a moonshot mission to reduce police-related gun violence by 50% over the course of 10 years.

Build VR Solutions for Social Good

Police primarily go through 40 hours of in-service training a year outside of the academy, and most of that time goes to topics like firearms and CPR recertification. There is not enough time to train on everything police need to be aware of. Officers who do learn a skill at in-service practice it once or twice, then are expected to remember it eight months later, under stress. Our goal is training that is more accessible, more memorable, and done more frequently. We call this "Roll Call" training: training that can be done before and after a shift to keep skills sharp.

Public-safety training is broken. Today's training is ineffective, not scalable, and expensive. Axon's VR team creates engaging, effective training with scenario feedback, including Community Engagement Training and less-lethal weapon training (like TASER), so officers are prepared to use alternatives to Use of Force.

Most police interactions are verbal and non-verbal, so we emphasize hand gestures and natural language processing. The trainee's body language, what they say, and how they say it all shape how they interact with NPCs (Non-Playable Characters) in the scenario. A trainer observes these interactions and gives feedback in a post-training debrief, and every product ties back into the Axon ecosystem through Axon Academy, Axon Evidence, Axon Performance, and Axon Standards.

Your Impact

You will join an interdisciplinary team tackling the biggest challenges in public safety training head-on, including immersive VR-based empathy, coping and de-escalation training that helps officers engage with the communities they serve with greater awareness and safety.

As one of the expanding members of Axon's VR team, the Senior Technical Character Artist is the bridge between art and technology for our NPCs. Because most training is a conversation, the believability of our characters carries the training. You will own character creation and character technology for our standalone-headset training simulators, from MetaHuman-based workflows to parametric clothing and materials, and help the rest of the art team deliver the best possible content under our technical restrictions. You will partner with Art, Engineering, Content, UX and User Research to deliver the best immersive quality for our trainings.

This is a senior role. We expect you to work independently, own your area end to end, and take direction from the Lead Technical Artist and the Art Director rather than needing day-to-day management.

SUMMARY: The position will be the Compliance Services department’s subject matter expert on the governing legal documents, as well as the Federal and local regulations they incorporate. The primary assignment is a compliance monitoring engagement, where the team monitors a residential property owner’s compliance with a federal Consent Decree (“CD”) covering the lead-based paint (“LBP”) inspection and abatement, substandard housing conditions, tenant relocation, rent abatement, and restitution. This is a hands-on generalist role. The position will interpret CD requirements, review compliance evidence, draft memos, test monitoring tools, and help launch special initiatives and programs.

The position will also support cross-department engagements and special projects as needed.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED : Operates under the direct general supervision of a Manager or Director.

ESSENTIAL DUITES AND RESPONSIBILITES: The below statements are intended to describe the general nature and scope of work being performed by this position. This is not a complete listing of all responsibilities, duties and/or skills required.

• Consent Decree and Regulatory Expertise

• Serve as the team’s expert on the CD, including its LBP, substandard conditions, relocation, rent abatement, restitution, and deliverable review provisions

• Interpret how the CD interacts with incorporated related requirements including but not limited to:

• EPA lead rules (40 C.F.R. Part 745, including abatement, clearance, and the RRP Rule)

• HUD’s Lead Safe Housing Rule (24 C.F.R. Part 35) and related inspection standards

• NYC Local Law 1 (Admin. Code §§ 27-2056.1-2056.18), the Housing Maintenance Code, Local Law 55 (indoor allergens), and NYC Health Code § 173

• Answer internal questions with cited, written analysis, and flag where the CD is silent or ambiguous

• Maintain the team’s reference library, FAQs, and requirement to citation crosswalks

• Track regulatory changes and assess their impact on CD obligations

• Compliance Monitoring and Review

• Review submissions and deliverables against established requirements and regulations

• Recommend whether to approve or disapprove submissions under the CD’s review process and track resubmission deadlines

• Review special program claims for eligibility, condition severity, repair deadlines, start and end dates, and calculation accuracy

• Request, track, and evaluate supporting documentation (e.g., tenant notices, EPA notifications, relocation records, contractor certifications, and approvals)

• Draft Action Plans, corrective action follow-up, and report narratives

• Support development of operational procedures

• Memos and Other Written Work Product

• Draft compliance memos, findings, deficiency notices, and correspondence to a variety of audiences

• Contribute sections to periodic reports

• Draft and redline program and operational policy language, reconciling competing drafts against established requirements and regulations

• Monitoring framework and tools

• Review and test compliance monitoring framework, checklists, trackers, and testing procedures for accuracy and completeness

• Trace each monitoring step back to its established requirement or regulation, and close gaps

• Test tools (e.g., Excel trackers, SharePoint lists and workflows, deadline calculations) with simple cases and document results

• Recommend process improvements and help maintain document management and audit-trail standards

• Program design and initiative support

• Support the design and rollout of initiatives (e.g., rent abatement program), including eligibility rules, procedures, intake forms, notices, review workflows, and controls

• Draft program guidance, FAQs and public-facing materials in plain language
